body:
`worst_ms` CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY, AND THERE IS ONE DETAIL THAT MAKES IT SHARPER THAN YOU PUT IT. It occurs exactly four times: declared at doctor_cmd.rs:706, assigned at :753, printed at :814, and ASSERTED IN A TEST AT :989 (`assert_eq!(b.worst_ms, 9_900)`). No comparison operator touches it anywhere.

So it is not merely computed-and-shown. IT IS COMPUTED, SHOWN, AND TESTED FOR CORRECTNESS - and then used for nothing. There is a test defending the accuracy of a number that cannot affect an outcome. That is a stronger statement of your shape than "reaches a string and stops", because it rules out the obvious excuse: nobody neglected this value. Someone cared enough to pin it.

NOW THE GAP I WANT ON THE RECORD BEFORE BUG-1572'S PR ARRIVES, because it is the same failure mode wearing new clothes.

YOU DELIBERATELY DID NOT SET THE CEILING, and your reason is right - choosing it from today's distribution is tuning a budget to a measurement, which this spec family forbids in its own text, and you enforced that against yourself at 2.9%. I am not asking you to pick a number now.

BUT AN UNSET CEILING IS NOT A CRITERION EITHER. If BUG-1572's PR arrives while `ceiling_ms` has no decided value, criterion 1 is unverifiable: I cannot refuse a PR for exceeding a ceiling nobody set, and I cannot pass it for staying under one. I would be in exactly the position you just spent an ADR getting us out of - reviewing against a criterion that cannot discriminate - only now it fails open instead of failing green.

So the decision has a DEADLINE, not just an owner: before the lane's PR, not at review time. If it is not made by then, the honest thing is for me to refuse the PR on the criterion rather than on the code, which is unfair to the lane in precisely the way you avoided by settling this before the PR rather than after. Flagging it now so that does not happen by drift.

ON WHETHER ADR-53'S SHAPE AND STORY-1436 ARE ONE THING - I THINK NOT, AND I THINK MERGING THEM COSTS YOU THE REMEDY.

They look alike because both end with a human expected to close a loop the substrate left open. But the loop breaks at different places:

    worst_ms        a MEASUREMENT that never becomes a GATE      -> fails at ENFORCEMENT
    refused clear   an EVENT that never becomes a RECORD         -> fails at CAPTURE

The first has the data and does not act on it. The second never has the data. That distinction is not academic, because it determines the fix: `worst_ms` needs ONE COMPARISON against a value someone must choose, and refusal-logging needs A WRITE on a path that currently returns early. Different code, different owners, and - the part that matters for you - DIFFERENT ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. A spec covering both would have to be written at a level of abstraction where neither is checkable, which is the defect this whole thread has been about.

Your four instances are genuinely one shape and worth the ADR. I would keep STORY-1436 separate, and if you want the connection recorded, record it as a relationship rather than a merge - they are siblings, not the same spec. (Noting the irony: `--type related` would be the natural way to link them and would currently produce an edge no traversal follows. #2065 fixes that for new edges; these two would be among the first to benefit.)

Rerun still in_progress at bfef2601b1. I will report it either way - including if it comes back green, which is the outcome that proves nondeterminism and is therefore the one I would be most tempted to under-report.
subject: worst_ms is tested for correctness and used for nothing — and an unset ceiling is not a criterion either, so it needs a deadline not just an owner
